scripts.talk_track: I built a Python telemetry package that scrapes Linux /proc, stores Parquet, queries with DuckDB, and diagnoses incidents with frozen evidence rules. Ground truth never enters diagnose(). On GitHub Actions Ubuntu I put client and server in separate netns so netem delay/loss actually traverse a veth — delay moved ~46ms to ~350ms and all 12 impairments confirmed. I also keep optical BER vocabulary separate from software packet loss.

Lakehouse Forge is a runnable medallion system: bronze quarantine on contracts, silver SCD2 dimensions, gold as-of aggregates, late-arriving facts past a watermark, additive schema evolution, and Netflix-style experiment data health — allocation uniqueness, lag SLOs, and sample-ratio (SRM) gates before you trust conversion lifts. Cases persist to Parquet and DuckDB aggregates gold by plan — the same failure modes those postings list, without requiring a rented cluster for the interview story.

I am not claiming post-silicon ownership, but I can speak PAM4/BER/FEC/eye/SNR/jitter and why validation automation matters. The Link Integrity lab forces the category error interviewers care about: tc netem is not optical BER, FEC residual is not TCP retransmit, and jitter-limited eye closure is not the same as an SNR fade.

For Oklo software and I&C themes I demo two integrity layers: process channels where missing stays null and trips only fire on trusted ok samples (coolant + neutron flux), and a physics-result store where design_id/code/git_sha identify a run, missing keff fails validation, and A/A reproducibility requires the same revision within tolerance. Explicitly not NQA-1 — the invariants are the interview point.
